metadata.title: SecOps-NG — CRA Essential Cybersecurity, Vulnerability Handling & Reporting Component Definition

components.title: SecOps-NG
components.description: SecOps-NG is a community-driven Digital Commons of portable security operations content (CACAO playbooks, OSCAL/D3FEND control mappings, OCSF data shapes, KPI/KRI catalog) plus reference compilers to n8n, Temporal, and LangGraph. This component definition exposes how the SecOps-NG content set addresses the CRA essential cybersecurity requirements: Annex I §1 (secure-by-design and secure-by-default product properties), Annex I §2 (vulnerability handling), and the manufacturer obligations of Article 13 (risk assessment, component due diligence, vulnerability-handling process, security-update dissemination, single point of contact), together with the manufacturer reporting obligations to the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA (Article 14).

control-implementations.description: Coverage of CRA (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) Annex I §1 essential cybersecurity requirements (secure-by-default configuration, access control, confidentiality, integrity, availability, attack-surface limitation, logging and monitoring, and security-update capability), Annex I §2 vulnerability-handling essential requirements (SBOM, vulnerability handling, coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, security update dissemination), Article 13 manufacturer obligations (risk assessment, component due diligence, vulnerability-handling process, security-update dissemination, and single point of contact), and Article 14 reporting obligations to the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA (early-warning, 72-hour notification, final report, severe-incident notification), as mapped in content/mappings/cra/annex-i-1-essential-cybersecurity.yaml, content/mappings/cra/article-13.yaml, and content/mappings/cra/article-14-and-annex-i.yaml.

implemented-requirements.description: Identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in the product with digital elements, including by drawing up a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format that covers at the very least the top-level dependencies.
Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates, and document the vulnerability-handling process throughout the support period.
Put in place and enforce a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, including a single point of contact for the receipt of information on vulnerabilities from any source.

Acknowledge receipt of a reported vulnerability to the reporter without undue delay, in accordance with the operator's documented coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure policy under Annex I §2(5). The acknowledgement window is set by the operator's CVD policy; ISO/IEC 29147 recommends three working days as the community baseline.

Ensure that, where technically feasible, security updates are disseminated without delay and free of charge for the duration of the support period, accompanied by advisory messages providing users with the relevant information.

Notify the CSIRT designated as coordinator and ENISA of any actively exploited vulnerability contained in the product without undue delay, and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of it (early-warning notification).

Notify the coordinator CSIRT and ENISA of any severe incident having an impact on the security of the product with digital elements, with early-warning (24h), notification (72h), and final report (1 month) timing analogous to Art. 14(1)–(2).

Products with digital elements shall ensure that vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates, including, where applicable, through automatic security updates that are installed within an appropriate timeframe enabled as a default setting, with a clear and easy-to-use opt-out mechanism, through the notification of available updates to users, and the option to temporarily postpone them.

Manufacturers shall undertake an assessment of the cybersecurity risks associated with the product with digital elements and take the outcome of that assessment into account during the planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance phases of the product, with a view to minimising cybersecurity risks, preventing security incidents and minimising the impacts of such incidents, including in relation to the health and safety of users.

When placing a product with digital elements on the market, manufacturers shall exercise due diligence when integrating components sourced from third parties so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product, including when integrating components of free and open-source software that have not been made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity.

When placing a product with digital elements on the market, manufacturers shall exercise due diligence when integrating components sourced from third parties so that those components do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product, including when integrating components of free and open-source software that have not been made available on the market in the course of a commercial activity.

Manufacturers shall systematically document, in a manner that is proportionate to the nature and the cybersecurity risks of the product, relevant cybersecurity aspects concerning the product with digital elements, including vulnerabilities of which they become aware and any relevant information provided by third parties.

Once a security update is available, manufacturers shall disseminate, in particular in cases of incidents resulting from the exploitation of a vulnerability, the available security updates without delay and, except for tailor-made products with digital elements, free of charge, accompanied by advisory messages providing users with the relevant information, including on potential action to be taken.

Manufacturers shall determine and document a support period during which vulnerabilities of the product with digital elements, including its components, are handled effectively. The period shall reflect the product's expected use, reasonable user expectations, the nature and intended purpose of the product, and the availability and support periods of its operating environment and core third-party components.

Manufacturers shall provide a single point of contact to enable users to communicate directly and rapidly with them, including in order to facilitate the reporting of vulnerabilities of the product with digital elements, and shall ensure that that single point of contact is easy to identify by users and available in one of the official languages of the Member States understandable to users.

Codebase-side vulnerability management for products with digital elements: walk the SBOM (Annex I §2(1)) against advisory feeds, remediate without delay (Annex I §2(2)), commit to a coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure policy (Annex I §2(5)), and disseminate security updates throughout the support period (Annex I §2(7)).
